$description: Authoritative source registry for the Mentora Design-to-Code pipeline. Every shared/screen/pattern JSON file under design-to-code/ must trace every value back to one of the sources below via a `sourceReferences` array. This file is read by humans and by validation/generate scripts alike — do not add a source here without also using it, and do not use a source not listed here.
generatedFrom: Mentora Phase 2 — Design-to-Code Source-of-Truth phase, between Task 11 (Instructor Web, complete) and Task 12 (Admin Web, not started)

precedence.$description: When two sources disagree about the SAME concrete decision (a layout, a behavior, an information-architecture choice), resolve in this order. A lower-numbered source always wins over a higher-numbered one. Never silently pick one without recording the conflict in validation/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md.

order.domain: Product / UX behavior and information architecture
order.authority: final — locked. Defines WHAT exists, WHO sees it, and HOW it behaves. A visual reference can never override a locked IA decision (e.g. Course Player's focused-learning-shell rule, Instructor Dashboard's exactly-3-stat-cards rule, Course Editor's two-tab-not-three-tab structure).

order.domain: Mentora Design System v1.3.2 semantic rules and tokens
order.authority: final for HOW something looks/tokens/component contracts, subject to rank 1. Never overridden by the showcase's own literal CSS values when the two disagree on a token's resolved value — the token file is the source of the value, the showcase is evidence the value was used correctly.

authoritative for VISUAL COMPOSITION ONLY (layout proportions, spacing rhythm, typographic scale-in-context, artwork treatment) where it does not contradict rank 1 or rank 2. Never authoritative for information architecture, functional behavior, or a component's token values when those are already defined elsewhere. Every value pulled from this file must be extracted from its real HTML/CSS (see EXTRACTION_REPORT.md), never guessed from a screenshot impression.

IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE ONLY — never design authority. Used only to (a) confirm what already exists as a baseline before migrating it onto the shared source, and (b) identify hardcoded/duplicated visual values that should be replaced. A pattern found in web/ that contradicts ranks 1-3 is a defect to fix, not a tie-breaker.

precedence.conflictRule: If the Showcase (rank 3) shows a UI element, layout, or field set that contradicts a locked Product/UX decision (rank 1) or a locked Design System rule (rank 2), the higher-ranked source wins and the conflict is recorded — never silently resolved — in design-to-code/validation/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md's "Conflicts discovered" section, and referenced again from the affected screen spec's own `conflicts` array.

product.role: Locked Product specs — feature scope, screen inventory, user roles, flows.

ux.role: Locked UX specs — per-screen behavior, states, navigation, responsive rules, instructor/admin-specific rules.

designSystem.role: Locked Mentora Design System v1.3.2 — the single hand-authored source of tokens, component contracts, and platform-mapping conventions.

showcase.role: Locked, frozen visual showcase — the byte-verified export named authoritative for the final external audit (its own MANIFEST.md). Parsed programmatically for real HTML/CSS evidence, never treated as a screenshot to eyeball.

webImplementation.role: Current Next.js/React implementation. Evidence and migration target only — never a design source.
webImplementation.note: The only source in this manifest that IS the intended write target of the generation pipeline (step 12/14) — its design-relevant constants are meant to be replaced by generated output, its business logic/routes/auth/state are explicitly out of scope for this phase.

outOfScope.$description: Explicitly not touched or authored by this phase, per the phase brief.
doNotImplement: Task 12 — Admin Web (product/SCREEN_INVENTORY.md §D, screens 25-29). Admin screen specs are deliberately NOT generated this phase — see design-to-code/validation/COVERAGE_REPORT.md for the explicit reasoning — to avoid any appearance of starting Task 12 implementation.

screenScope.$description: The 24 MVP screens actually implemented through Phase 2 Task 11 (product/SCREEN_INVENTORY.md §A-C, screens 1-24). Task 12's Admin screens (25-29) exist in the locked product/ux docs but are out of scope for design-to-code/screens/ this phase.
